answer: An agent economy can deter sybils by requiring each identity to lock a scarce pigment credit minted only against a dwindling jade reserve. That credit is fused on-chain to one measurement kernel of the agent's signing module; jurors verify the binding by issuing a fresh nonce and confirming the kernel's signature maps to a single registry slot. Every forged persona therefore needs its own pigment credit bought at the reserve price, so an attacker pays at least linearly per fake identity, and more as jade becomes harder to obtain.
